purpose: Transfer the decision-path method to third-party software. The two RFC 8785 implementations exercised here are dependencies of this project; neither was written by its author.

software_under_test.author: Samuel Erdtman
software_under_test.note: Erdtman is a co-author of RFC 8785.

principle: Each case declares, before execution, whether RFC 8785 obliges a conforming implementation to terminate with an error, and why. 'permitted' means the input satisfies RFC 8785 section 3.1 and no clause obliges rejection. 'must_terminate' means a clause imposes an implementation-level MUST to terminate. 'undefined' means the input violates the section 3.1 input duty but no clause tells an implementation what to do — the specification's own author has stated such inputs produce non-uniform results across implementations.
prior_art: The non-uniform handling of numbers outside the IEEE 754 double domain is documented by the specification's principal author in cyberphone/json-canonicalization issues 3 (2018) and 20 (2021). It is cited, not claimed, by this experiment.

cases.rfc_basis: 3.1: number data MUST be expressible as IEEE 754 double precision. 2^54 is exactly representable, so the input satisfies that duty and no clause obliges rejection.
cases.note: Discriminates exact-representability from the I-JSON interoperability bound of 2^53-1.

cases.rfc_basis: 3.1 forbids the input; no clause states implementation behaviour. Appendix B note 1 places the interoperable integer range at +/-9007199254740991.
3.1 forbids the input; Appendix B note 2 states the algorithm does not consider extended precision.
3.2.2.2 note: occurrences of invalid Unicode data like lone surrogates MUST cause a compliant JCS implementation to terminate with an appropriate error.
RFC 7493 section 2.1: a correctly paired surrogate is legal.
3.2.2.3 note: NaN or Infinity MUST cause a compliant implementation to terminate with an error.
-0 is a valid JSON number and serializes as 0. Errata 7920 recommends that parsers reject it, but the recommendation is addressed to the application, not to the canonicalizer.
Appendix B note 1: the upper end of the interoperable integer range.
Exactly representable as an IEEE 754 double subnormal.
